articles.title: Libertarians challenge Trump-backed Republicans, look to shake up midterms beyond GOP-Dem duopoly

paras.en: In the American political scene dominated by the GOP-Democrat duopoly, Libertarians like Kentucky congressional candidate Jeremy Todd are looking to offer voters an alternative as they head to the polls during the midterm elections.

"I think ultimately the Republican Party has abandoned… true conservatism, small government principles," Todd told Fox News Digital this week, asserting that "they may be more conservative than Democrats, but, to us true conservatives, that's not good enough."

Todd, who views himself as "right of MAGA," mounted his long-shot U.S. House bid after Rep. Thomas Massie lost the Republican primary in Kentucky's 4th Congressional District to Trump-backed former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein. Democratic congressional candidate Melissa Strange is also running in the contest.

"We are welcoming people who are conservative, who believe in small, limited government, to my campaign and then to a larger movement that is probably gonna need to exist post the downfall of the Republican Party," Todd said.
Former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent, who quit his post earlier this year due to his opposition to the Iran war, and former Rep. Ron Paul, have both backed Todd.

In a Pew Research survey of U.S. adults released earlier this month, 5% of registered voters indicated that they would vote for another candidate other than the GOP and Democratic candidates in the U.S. House race in their district, while 15% were not sure about how they would vote. The poll, carried out Sept. 28-Oct. 4, had a margin of error among registered voters of plus or minus 1.8 percentage points.
Todd is not the only Libertarian running this election cycle looking to make an impact — but no candidate running under the Libertarian Party has ever been elected to the U.S. Congress.

Former Rep. Justin Amash of Michigan, who switched from Republican to Independent and then to Libertarian during his final term, became "the first LP member to serve in Congress," according to the Libertarian National Committee — but Amash, who served in the House for a decade, won all of his elections as a Republican.
Libertarian candidate Ted Brown is on the ballot for the 2026 Texas U.S. Senate race that features Trump-backed state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico.

Brown earned only about 2.36% of the vote in the 2024 Texas U.S. Senate contest won by incumbent GOP Sen. Ted Cruz. He dismissed the criticism he says he gets regularly from Republicans that he is merely spoiling Paxton’s chances.
"They could avoid that problem by nominating a better candidate," Brown said, noting that he delivers the same message to Democrats.
"You can’t spoil a system that’s already rotten," Brown stated. "There are a lot of people making a protest vote, and there’s good reason to."

Bill Redpath, a former Libertarian National Committee (LNC) chair who is currently listed as an at-large LNC representative, is running in the special Ohio U.S. Senate race where Trump-backed Republican Sen. Jon Husted faces former Sen. Sherrod Brown, a Democrat.
Redpath earned less than 2% of the vote in a 2022 Illinois U.S. Senate bid.
Todd, while speaking to Fox News Digital, urged voters not to "buy into the lesser of two evils talk. Make sure you get out there and vote and give us a real shot because we can win this."

Todd, who supports Massie's bid to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth and the congressman's push to pass the Epstein Files Transparency Act II, is a fiscal hawk who advocates slashing government spending to address the much-discussed "affordability" issue.
"The affordability crisis is not a hoax," he said, suggesting that younger individuals particularly face this "stark reality."

"The only answer is we've got to cut government spending so that we stop money printing, so that we stop debasing and devaluing the currency and their wages have an opportunity to catch up. That's ultimately what's happening is we're printing money faster than wages can keep up with and it's kind of left an entire generation behind to the benefit of asset holders," Todd said.

"The easiest way you can cut government spending is get out of these stupid conflicts. We should not be paying billions of dollars to Ukraine to fight Russia. We should not be paying billions of dollars to come to Israel's defense," Todd asserted. "And last but not least, we should get out of this conflict in Iran. Just leave."
In a Sunday post on X, Todd called President Trump "a warmonger."

During the Fox News Digital interview, Todd credited Trump with forging "the greatest coalition we've maybe ever seen in politics," noting that Trump delivered a speech at the Libertarian National Convention in 2024 to appeal to the voting bloc.

"We believe that the job of the United States military is not to wage endless regime-change wars around the globe," Trump told that Libertarian gathering in 2024, but "to defend America from attack and invasion here at home."
Todd said since delivering that speech, Trump has gone "back on all but essentially one of the promises, which is border security."
"We've not gotten deportations to the level that we wanted. We've gotten into another stupid and maybe the biggest and most ridiculous Middle Eastern conflict," Todd said.
The White House did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

In a statement provided to Fox News Digital, Republican National Committee national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre declared, "President Trump has endorsed Ed Gallrein, a Navy SEAL and fifth-generation farmer who will represent the needs of working families in Congress. Republicans are focused on electing America First Republicans in Kentucky and around the country."

Trump, who has been traveling to various states to campaign for Republican candidates amid midterm election season, rallied in Kentucky's 4th Congressional District earlier this month, blasting Massie as "the worst."
Fox News Digital reached out to Massie to find out whether he'll vote in the congressional race, and, if so, how he will cast his ballot.
"I won't be voting for the AIPAC candidate," Massie tersely texted Fox News Digital, referring to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee.

Reports indicate that millions in AIPAC-linked funds were poured into the primary, with The New York Times saying, "This year, one of the group’s most high-profile wins was the ouster of Mr. Massie, a seven-term congressman who has called for ending military aid to Israel."
AIPAC did not provide comment to Fox News Digital for this report.

The Gallrein campaign responded to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on Massie with the following statement: "It is tragically fitting that his last act as congressman would be to once again, turn his back on his district and his party by siding with radical Democrats. This is exactly why voters fired him in May."
In an interview with a local news station, Todd said he would never run against Massie, but now, he’s "running for him."
The Associated Press contributed to this report

articles.title: Dead felon voting controversy grows as 'Betty No Last Name' surfaces in Spanberger's rights restoration push

paras.en: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger’s effort to restore voting rights to tens of thousands of convicted felons sparked controversy Thursday after an attorney obtained an executive citation addressed to "Betty No Last Name," purportedly notifying the recipient that her voting rights had been restored.

The citation identifies No Last Name as one of more than 66,000 Virginians whose rights to vote, serve on juries and seek public office have reportedly been restored under Spanberger's administration. The controversy comes ahead of a Nov. 3 ballot measure that would make voting rights restoration automatic upon release from prison.
"It’s a big deal," said Virginia Beach attorney Tim Anderson, who first obtained the citation for No Last Name and shared it with Fox News Digital.

"It’s clear [Spanberger] didn’t sign it. No governor and no secretary of the commonwealth would sign a restoration order that says Betty No Last Name, so they’re not looking at it; they didn’t review anything," Anderson told Fox News Digital in an interview Thursday. Each citation bears the signatures of the governor and Secretary of the Commonwealth Candi Mundon-King.
"Whereas, Betty No Last Name, by reason of conviction(s), suffers political disabilities …," the citation obtained by Fox News Digital says.

Anderson said he obtained the citation through a public records request to the Chesapeake Sheriff's Office after reports emerged that restoration notices had been sent to felons who are now deceased. He said the document originated from Spanberger's office and was sent to the sheriff's office.
He speculated that the citations were generated through a mail merge of records and signed using an autopen despite language in the documents indicating that each case had been individually reviewed.
Former Virginia Attorney General Jason Miyares also questioned whether the administration had individually reviewed the restoration cases.
"Four mentions of ‘Betty No Last Name’ and still no last name. I’m thinking perhaps Abigail Spanberger’s ‘individualized review’ is just imaginary," Miyares said in a statement.

Fox News Digital reached out to Spanberger, Mundon-King and the Chesapeake Sheriff's Office for comment. A sheriff's office official said she was not immediately familiar with the case but would look into it.

Anderson said he found the questionable citation after contacting only a handful of Virginia law enforcement agencies and believes similar cases may exist elsewhere in the state. He also suggested that officials whose signatures appear on the citations could face criminal liability if the documents were found to be fraudulent, potentially resulting in forfeiture of office.
Anderson’s finding went viral on social media Thursday, and critics pointed out how No Last Name’s citation colored the upcoming ballot question on automatic rights restoration for felons.

Some Virginia lawmakers have called for an independent audit of Spanberger's rights-restoration process. State Sen. Glen Sturtevant, R-Chesterfield, who has called for the audit, said reports have since emerged of restoration citations being sent to deceased individuals.
"Now a certificate for "Betty No Last Name," signed by the governor. Still no audit. Vote no on Question 3," Sturtevant said in a statement.
"Congratulations to Betty No Last Name," added Del. Wren Williams, R-Stuart. "You can now vote in Virginia."

articles.title: Cuts like a knife: Canadian rocker Bryan Adams trolls Trump with new song
articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

paras.en: Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says Canadian rock star Bryan Adams, is Lake America.
In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump, accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores.

Trump signed an executive order in August directing US federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America”, echoing his earlier, widely mocked decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico “the Gulf of America”.

The move further escalated a feud with Canada that has strained the longstanding alliance between the two countries. Trump’s decision has largely been met with derision in Canada, with some pointing out that the province of Ontario is named after the lake, not the other way around. Adams’ lyrics emphasise the roots of the name:
The ‘lake of shining waters’ is what the Iroquois called her
It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order.

Adams’s lyrics also suggest that Trump’s naming stunt was intended to deflect from the president’s other political problems, including the war in Iran and renewed scrutiny of the Jeffrey Epstein files.
But things weren’t going his way in Iran
So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram
While the Epstein files were getting traction

The song is part of what Adams described in a recent interview as a broader “love letter” to Canada: a songwriting project that began with an invitation from a film company to write about the Maritimes provinces of Canada and has since morphed into the upcoming album How’s It Goin’.
“After finishing the first song, I moved on to that one, and then moved on to another one, and then started thinking maybe I should just carry on with my theme,” he said.
As well as homages to Canadian heroes, the album also includes 51st State, released on 1 July – Canada Day – as another repudiation of Trump, in this case his efforts to annex Canada.
The first time he played the song in public was in the US.
“We weren’t sure how people were going to respond to it,” he said. “But we got a standing ovation every night for it. It made me think: perhaps, finally, the tide’s turning.”

articles.title: Israel election results: Qatar says accusations of election interference in Israel ‘ridiculous and dangerous’ – as it happened
articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now); Taz Ali and Jonathan Yerushalmy (earlier)

paras.en: Qatar says accusations of election interference in Israel 'ridiculous and dangerous'
Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections.
“We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.
“They accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote... These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”
That’s all from me, Tom Ambrose, and from the Israel election results live blog for today.
Here is a round-up of today’s headlines:

Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power, after he claimed that Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which the prime minister’s coalition lost its parliamentary majority. Netanyahu and his allies called on the internal security service, Shin Bet, to investigate alleged vote buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities in Israel, supposedly funded by foreign money.

Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the main opposition bloc, accused the prime minister and his Likud party of trying to derail the election results. “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election,” Eisenkot said in a video message.

Netanyahu’s allegations were quickly disowned by a range of government officials, including police officers and members of the election committee. He was also rebuked by the president for “tarnishing an entire community”. On Wednesday night, the prime minister posted a statement by Likud online which described the claimed violations as “an attack on democracy whose purpose is to lead to a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamisation of Israel, and the overthrow of rightwing rule”.

Opposition leaders lambasted the claims of Netanyahu, 77, who has run Israel for 19 of the past 30 years. Yousef Jabareen, the Joint List leader, accused the prime minister of incitement. “Netanyahu was defeated at the ballot box,” Jabareen said, adding that he “refuses to come to terms with the fact that the Arab public voted and decided”.

Ahmad Tibi, one of the leaders of the Joint List party, said Benjamin Netanyahu was on an orchestrated, toxic campaign meant to undermine the election results. “This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra’am,” Tibi told Reuters.

Meanwhile, Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections. “We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.

Iran attempted to interfere in the Israeli election this week and will try to disrupt the US midterm elections next week, the Telegraph reports. “We have been looking into ways to recruit agents in both the American and Israeli regimes’ election processes,” one official said, adding that “powerful cyber groups have also been established to hack their election systems”.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz has reported that, with 97% of votes counted, the balance between the political blocs remains unchanged. Netanyahu’s coalition remains at 53 seats and Eisenkot’s bloc at 48. Parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel hold 19 seats. The final tally of absentee ballots is not expected to significantly shift the results, with no grouping managing to reach the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.

Mahmoud Abbas, the president of the Palestinian Authority, expressed hope that the Israeli election would pave the way for renewed peace talks. “For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace,” Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia.

The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog, has come to the defence of Palestinian voters, as he urged political leaders against “tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote”. He saidShin Bet and the country’s central elections committee would investigate allegations of foreign interference “throughly”.

The central elections committee’s acting director general, Dean Livne, said there was “no basis for claims of systematic violations of election integrity”. The Israeli police also dismissed the claims, according to comments reported in Hebrew-language media, with one source quoted as saying: “Election day passed with very few irregular incidents.”

Israel’s chief opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot has warned that prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu was working to delegitimise election results with his allegations of malfeasance by parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel that performed well.

“It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election,” Eisenkot said in a video message, referring to the prime minister’s right-wing party.

Supreme Court justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Elections Committee, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that Ra’am received money from Qatar.
“The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said.
Ra’am chief Mansour Abbas said his party had “no connection whatsoever to the affair” and welcomed an investigation.
Iran tried to interfere with Israeli election - report
Iran attempted to interfere in the Israeli election this week and will try to disrupt the US midterm elections next week, the Telegraph reports.

“We have been looking into ways to recruit agents in both the American and Israeli regimes’ election processes,” one official said, adding that “powerful cyber groups have also been established to hack their election systems”.
Meanwhile, another official described it as an extension of its war with the US and Israel.

“War does not just mean missiles and guns when we are under their blockade,” he said. “It also means we are prepared to disrupt their elections, their banking, their travel and all their ordinary systems. We are not in favour of any candidate anywhere, but we would like to see a divided America and a divided Israel.”
Ahmad Tibi, one of the leaders of the Joint List party, said Benjamin Netanyahu was on an orchestrated, toxic campaign meant to undermine the election results.
“This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra’am,” Tibi told Reuters.

During and after Tuesday’s election, Netanyahu and his allies warned against rising Arab turnout and his right-wing Likud party issued statements accusing the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel of “stealing the vote.“

It demanded police and the Shin Bet domestic intelligence service investigate incidents of suspected election bribery and intimidation at ballot stations. It said it possessed evidence of such activity but has not presented it to the public.
Abbas expresses hope for dialogue with new Israeli government
Mahmoud Abbas, the president of the Palestinian Authority, expressed hope that the Israeli election would pave the way for renewed peace talks.

“For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace,” Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia.
“We hope that, immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we will be able to engage in dialogue together.”
As vote counting continues in Israel, here is a roundup of today’s key developments:

Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies have amplified allegations of election fraud against parties representing Palestinian citizens in Israel. He and members of his coalition have referred the parties to Shin Bet, the country’s domestic security service, for investigation. Netanyahu’s Likud party accused the Palestinian parties of “stealing” the election and claimed, without evidence, that they received money from Qatar.

Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, rejected the allegations, saying they were “ridiculous and dangerous”. Responding to the claims, he said: “We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome.”

The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog, has come to the defence of Palestinian voters, as he urged political leaders against “tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote”. He saidShin Bet and the country’s central elections committee would investigate allegations of foreign interference “throughly”.

The central elections committee’s acting director general, Dean Livne, said there was “no basis for claims of systematic violations of election integrity”. The Israeli police also dismissed the claims, according to comments reported in Hebrew-language media, with one source quoted as saying: “Election day passed with very few irregular incidents.”

Netanyahu’s chief rival, former military chief and Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, warned political opponents against exploiting allegations of foreign interference to delay the swearing-in of the next Knesset, which is set for 10 November.

The sentiment was shared by Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, who accused Netanyahu of trying to “undermine the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign” targeting Palestinian citizens in Israel.
So far, Netanyahu’s bloc is projected to win 53 seats, compared with 48 for the grouping led by rival Eisenkot. Palestinian parties are projected to win 19 seats, a record high.
The final tally of absentee ballots is not expected to significantly shift the results, with no grouping managing to reach the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.
Qatar says accusations of election interference in Israel 'ridiculous and dangerous'
Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections.
“We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.
“They accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote... These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”
Both Benjamin Netanyahu and his immediate challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, lack the seats in the Knesset to form a majority government. Eisenkot and his allies face a clear choice.

They could forge a pact with the Arab Israeli parties, currently heading for an historic 19 seats, which would allow them to vote Netanyahu out and form a governing coalition. Or they could enter a unity government with Netanyahu, in return for a ministry or two.

Likud officials are cited in today’s Israeli press as saying Eisenkot will ultimately have no option but to throw in his lot with Netanyahu. Other observers say that would be political suicide, especially as the opposition leader vowed in the campaign he would never collaborate with the prime minister.
However, Eisenkot and key members of his bloc have also ruled out cooperation with the Arab party lists. Breaking either pledge would be costly for them.

The prime minister’s attack on the legitimacy of the Palestinian vote is designed to tip the scales, to force Eisenkot into the Netanyahu camp by increasing the political toxicity of any arrangement with Arab parties, the Joint List and Ra’am.

For its part, the Joint List has ruled out participating in an Eisenkot government because of his bloc’s support for the war in Gaza and the occupation of southern Lebanon, but it has offered to support an Eisenkot minority government with tactical voting in the new Knesset, in the shared interest of ousting Netanyahu.

Even such a transactional arrangement is hard to achieve given the state of Israeli Jewish politics. The only Zionist party that advocates cooperation with Palestinians, the Democrats, won just 6.5% of the total vote by the latest count.
The right and centre-right accounted for 66.5%, while ultra-orthodox Jewish parties won 11%.

Against that background, Eisenkot has doubled down on his determination to form a Zionist government. Such rhetoric makes the prospect of cooperation with Arab parties even more remote, but he is hoping instead to lure away conservative Jews from Likud, just as Netanyahu’s is trawling for defectors from Eisenkot’s “Change” bloc.
This is the current phase of the post-election struggle, and it is one that, for now, excludes Arab Israelis, despite their dramatically increased political strength.

The head of one of Israel’s parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel rejected allegations of electoral fraud and welcomed an investigation, saying his moderate Islamist Ra’am party had “no connection” to the matter.

“Ra’am has no connection whatsoever to the affair in question or to any other affairs, and we declare that we will fully cooperate with all law enforcement authorities to uncover the truth,” Mansour Abbas said, according to a spokesperson for his party.
Analysis: Netanyahu cries foul as Palestinian parties in Israel surge

The race to form a government in Israel has begun with characteristically brass-knuckle tactics from Benjamin Netanyahu. He and other members of his coalition have referred the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, the only part of the opposition which over-performed in Tuesday’s elections, to the country’s domestic security service, the Shin Bet, for investigation.

The government’s claims centre around the allegation that Qatari funds were used illegally to buy votes and mobilise Palestinian Israeli citizens. There is so far no evidence to support the accusation. Haaretz quotes a senior police official saying there were no signs of election fraud and that Tuesday’s vote was cleaner than usual.

In Nazareth on election day, it was clear that turnout was unusually high because of anxiety and fear of what actions the extremists in Netanyahu’s government might turn their attention to Palestinian communities in Israel if they continue in power.

The only reported irregularities involved the the ruling coalition. Many of the ballots delivered to the polling station were printed only in Hebrew, while monitors from the far right used a variety of ploys to slow down the vote.
There is also a certain irony underpinning the allegations as Netanyahu is mired in a scandal over Qatari payments to his advisers in return for improving the Gulf monarchy’s image.
'We must avoid tarnishing an entire community,' says Herzog in defence of Palestinian vote

Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, has come to the defence of Palestinian voters in the Israeli election, amid accusations by Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies of alleged ballot fraud by parties representing Palestinian voters of Israel.

Herzog said he has spoken to the heads of the country’s central elections committee and Shin Bet regarding allegations of foreign interference in Tuesday’s vote, saying the issue must be “thoroughly investigated”.
“I am closely following developments in the investigation into the suspicions reported this morning,” he said in remarks published by Israeli media.
He added: “But even at a moment like this, we must avoid tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy.”
Herzog called on party representatives ahead of impending coalition talks to reconsider their positions out of a sense of responsibility towards the country.

Once the official results are in, I will meet with representatives of all the political groups. I say this to everyone here – to the public and its leaders – ahead of next week’s consultations: keep an open mind, keep an open heart and broaden your perspective.
There is only one question that should be at the forefront of your minds: what is in the best interests of the country?”
Palestinian party leader accuses Netanyahu of laying groundwork to reject election results
A Palestinian party leader in Israel has accused Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies of undermining the legitimacy of “the clearest election results Israel has seen in decades”.

Sami Abu Shehadeh, chair of the Balad party which forms part of the Arab-led Joint List, said unsubstantiated allegations of foreign interference in the election sought to delegitimise the Palestinian vote.

What began with the illegal disqualification of Arab parties escalated into incitement against Arab parties and the Arab public. On election day, hundreds of far-right activists armed with weapons were deployed at polling stations in Arab towns in an attempt to suppress voter turnout. Now, this racist blood libel is entering its next phase, fuelled by dangerous accusations.
Netanyahu and his allies are dangerous. They are laying the groundwork to reject the clearest election results Israel has seen in decades.”
He added that Netanyahu, as “a man charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust”, was inciting against the Palestinian citizens of Israel, which make up 20% of the population.

In any functioning democracy, those who lose an election accept responsibility and step down. In Israel, the losing side manufactures a racist blood libel and calls on the security forces to use force to overturn the people’s verdict.
We must not let the far right steal the election or drag the country into another election on the basis of fabricated, delusional accusations.

Echoing Ben-Gvir, the far-right Israeli finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, has also called on Shin Bet to interrogate the leaders of parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, amid claims of alleged foreign election interference that critics say risk casting suspicion on the Arab vote.
“The suspicion of election manipulation using foreign Islamist money is a litmus test for the State of Israel,” Smotrich said on X.
“The heads of the Arab parties must be interrogated by the Shin Bet today.”
Golan accuses Netanyahu of 'ugly delegitimisation campaign' against Palestinian voters

Hot on Eisenkot’s heels, Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, has accused Benjamin Netanyahu of trying to “undermine the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign” targeting Palestinian citizens in Israel.
Netanyahu’s Likud party has claimed – without evidence – that parties representing these citizens have “stolen” the election and demanded the police and the Shin Bet investigate the allegations.
Netanyahu suffered a crushing democratic defeat. The public fired him, and he refuses to accept the verdict of the voters.
Now he is trying to undermine the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign against the will of the public, and against the Arab public in particular.
Any genuine suspicion of damage to the integrity of the elections must be investigated to the end.”

Israel’s central elections committee has requested the Shin Bet to investigate alleged foreign interference, the Associated Press reported, citing claims in a letter dated Wednesday of funding by “foreign entities against the Israeli interest” but providing no details or assessment of their validity. The source of the allegations remains unclear, and the committee has requested findings within a week, ahead of the 4 November deadline for certifying election results under Israeli law.

articles.title: Hong Kong’s leader apologises for residential fire that killed 168 people
articles.author: Guardian reporter

paras.en: Hong Kong’s leader has apologised for government shortcomings that contributed to a fire that killed 168 people in the city last year, a rare sign of public contrition that nevertheless failed to impress some victims’ families.
The chief executive, John Lee, and seven other officials bowed in apology at the release of a report that pointed to “decades of failure” by government bodies.
Four departments “should bear part of the responsibility” for the high casualties, the report said. So far one official, housing secretary Winnie Ho, has resigned.

Last November, a small fire probably started by a cigarette grew into an inferno that enveloped seven of the eight towers in Wang Fuk Court, a housing complex that was shrouded in bamboo scaffolding and netting for renovations.

Former residents and victims’ families have been waiting to see how the government will address who is to blame for the ignored warnings, substandard building materials and disabled fire alarms that made the fire the world’s deadliest in a residential building since 1980.
Authorities have filed charges, including manslaughter, against seven individuals and two companies over their roles in the fire. At least 35 people have been arrested.
The independent report released on Thursday found the “main culprits” of the fire were private contractors but also accused officials of “lax enforcement”.

Had the four departments better recognised the risks and acted accordingly, “there was a real possibility that the misconduct of the private-sector parties and the fire hazards in WF Court could have been rectified or removed before the fire”, it said.
Lee said a three-month investigation would now begin into the government’s role.
“I am deeply saddened. I would like to apologise to the affected residents and the general public,” Lee said on Thursday, adding that housing minister Ho should “bear political responsibility”.

But Yip Ka-kui, who lost his wife and home in the fire, told reporters he did not consider the government’s acceptance of accountability adequate. “All the secretaries for the departments named should step down,” he said, according to AFP news agency. “Administrative responsibility falls short” and political accountability even more so, Yip added.
Phyllis Lo, whose mother died in the fire, told AP news agency that progress had been made but that justice had yet to be served.
She added the officials’ apology was late, though it was better than nothing.
Hong Kong’s government has previously been accused by critics of being more concerned with clamping down on criticism rather than addressing the causes of the disaster.
Since a National Security Law was imposed on the city in 2020 by Beijing, the city’s once vibrant civil society groups and political opposition have been all but quashed.
In the weeks after the fire, authorities warned against crimes that “exploit the tragedy” and reportedly arrested at least three people for sedition.
China’s national security agency in Hong Kong also summoned international media representatives, saying they had smeared the government in their reports on the fire.
On Thursday Lee promised that ““similar incidents will never be allowed to happen again”.
Some observers had called for a more legally powerful inquiry commission to be set up, rather than the judge-led independent review committee that compiled Thursday’s report.
Lee told reporters that authorities had proposed “systematic reforms”, including criminalising bid-rigging and overhauling the complaints system.
The report stated: “The fire has been put out, but the reform has only just begun.”

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss

paras.en: The defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States.
paras.zh: 在巴西总统大选中落败的候选人弗莱维奥·博尔索纳罗（ Flévio Bolsonaro ）在离开巴西前往美国后在社交媒体上发表的一封信中称自己为“巴西领导人”。

paras.en: Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat.
paras.zh: 博尔索纳罗在周日的决赛中以440万票的差异输给了他的左翼对手路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（ Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ） ，但没有承认失败。

paras.en: In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.
paras.zh: 在信中，博尔索纳罗在没有提供证据的情况下声称他是“选举欺诈”的受害者，并表示他将领导美国的反对派。

paras.en: He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".
paras.zh: 在未能遵守交出护照的命令后，他于周二离开了巴西，卢拉称这一决定是“可耻的行为”。

paras.en: Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".
paras.zh: 博尔索纳罗在信的开头写道： “作为巴西的领导人，我向巴西人民和国际社会发表讲话。”

paras.en: However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."
paras.zh: 然而，他发布了之前的版本，后来被删除，他在其中写道： “我作为巴西的合法总统向巴西人民和国际社会发表讲话。”

paras.en: Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.
paras.zh: 这两个版本都重复了博尔索纳罗在选举之夜首次提出的指控，即周日投票时间的延长使他的竞争对手受益。

paras.en: In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".
paras.zh: 他在信中说，这是“在我眼前展开的选举舞弊”。

paras.en: The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.
paras.zh: 卢拉和博尔索纳罗的竞选团队都要求延期，巴西选举当局负责人表示，投票过程正常，完全符合该国的法律和宪法。

paras.en: An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.
paras.zh: BBC巴西和BBC Verify对选举数据的分析还发现，在延长的时间内，只有约34,000人投票-远低于卢拉与博尔索纳罗之间的440万票。

paras.en: In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours.
paras.zh: 博尔索纳罗在信中还谈到了他离开巴西的情况，这在他失踪超过24小时后引起了混乱。

paras.en: It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador.
paras.zh: 后来发现，他在厄瓜多尔短暂停留加油后，越过陆地边界前往阿根廷，并从那里飞往佛罗里达州。

paras.en: Bolsonaro left after failing to hand in his passports to police - in defiance of a Supreme Court order, which had been issued as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering.
paras.zh: Bolsonaro在没有向警方交出护照后离开了-无视最高法院的命令，该命令是作为对涉嫌洗钱的调查的一部分发布的。

paras.en: He has not been charged as part of the money laundering probe and denies any wrongdoing, calling the investigation a "politically-motivated witch hunt".
paras.zh: 他没有被指控为洗钱调查的一部分，并否认有任何不当行为，称调查是“出于政治动机的猎巫”。

paras.en: Bolsonaro added that he had never intended to leave Brazil, but argued that he was the victim of "political persecution".
paras.zh: 博尔索纳罗补充说，他从未打算离开巴西，但他认为自己是“政治迫害”的受害者。

paras.en: He ended the letter by saying: "I left Brazil but I haven't abandoned Brazilians".
paras.zh: 他在信的最后说： “我离开了巴西，但我没有抛弃巴西人”。

paras.en: While FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro said that he planned to lead the opposition from the US, it was not clear how he planned to do that.
paras.zh: 虽然弗莱维奥·博尔索纳罗（ Flávio Bolsonaro ）表示他计划领导美国的反对派，但目前尚不清楚他计划如何做到这一点。

paras.en: His party recognised the election result and while some of its politicians have described Bolsonaro as a "political exile", his campaign manager, RogÃ©rio Marinho, stated on Wednesday that "there is no evidence" of the electoral fraud that Bolsonaro alleges took place.
paras.zh: 他的政党承认选举结果，虽然其一些政客将博尔索纳罗描述为“政治流亡者” ，但他的竞选经理RogérioMarinho周三表示， “没有证据”表明博尔索纳罗声称发生了选举舞弊。

paras.en: It is also not yet clear where Bolsonaro intends to stay or for how long.
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚博尔索纳罗打算在哪里停留或停留多久。

paras.en: His younger brother, Eduardo, has been in self-imposed exile in the US since March 2025, saying he was the victim of political persecution. The two siblings posted a photo of themselves holding a Brazilian flag on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 他的弟弟爱德华多自2025年3月以来一直在美国流亡，称他是政治迫害的受害者。两兄弟姐妹周三发布了一张自己举着巴西国旗的照片。

paras.en: The Trump administration has provided visas for FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro and his family but did not say what kind of visas they were.
paras.zh: 特朗普政府为Flávio Bolsonaro及其家人提供了签证，但没有说明他们是哪种签证。

paras.en: The US president did not explicitly endorse Bolsonaro in the run-up to the election and told reporters he "won't get involved" when asked about Bolsonaro's allegations of election fraud.
paras.zh: 在选举前夕，美国总统没有明确支持博尔索纳罗，并告诉记者，当被问及博尔索纳罗关于选举舞弊的指控时，他“不会介入”。

paras.en: Earlier in the week, he had said that "it looked like another rigged election," without providing any evidence.
paras.zh: 本周早些时候，他曾表示“这看起来像是又一次被操纵的选举” ，但没有提供任何证据。

paras.en: And on Thursday, Trump told reporters that "the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil".
paras.zh: 周四，特朗普告诉记者， “这次选举对巴西人民来说是一个非常大的尴尬”。

articles.title: Alaska governor orders probe into Democratic campaign's alleged links to same-name candidate

paras.en: The Republican governor of Alaska has ordered an investigation into an alleged "scheme" which led to two Dan Sullivans standing in the state's US Senate race.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加州共和党州长已下令对所谓的“计划”进行调查，该计划导致两名丹·沙利文参加该州的美国参议院竞选。

paras.en: Governor Mike Dunleavy said he was responding to a New York Times (NYT) story, external which said the team of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.
paras.zh: 州长迈克·邓利维（ Mike Dunleavy ）表示，他正在回应《纽约时报》（ NYT ）的一篇外部报道，该报道称，民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉（ Mary Peltola ）的团队与那些试图在参议院竞选中招募扰乱者候选人的人合作。

paras.en: The governor's post on X said he would investigate "whether this scheme violated Alaska's laws". He did not say which laws he had in mind.
paras.zh: 州长在X的帖子中表示，他将调查“该计划是否违反了阿拉斯加州的法律”。他没有说他想到了哪些法律。

paras.en: Dan Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters. Peltola's team deny any wrongdoing.
paras.zh: 现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文（ Dan Sullivan ）及其盟友指责民主党人试图混淆选民。佩尔托拉的团队否认有任何不当行为。

paras.en: They say they did not encourage the second Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher who lives in a remote fishing village, to stand. He has denied any links with the Peltola campaign.
paras.zh: 他们说，他们没有鼓励第二位住在偏远渔村的退休教师丹·沙利文（ Dan Sullivan ）站起来。他否认与佩尔托拉运动有任何联系。

paras.en: The Alaska race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest of the upcoming US midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress. Americans head to the polls across the country on Tuesday.
paras.zh: 分析人士认为，阿拉斯加竞选是即将举行的美国中期选举中最紧张的一次，这将决定哪个政党控制国会。周二，美国人前往全国各地的民意调查。

paras.en: Dunleavy's statement, which did not name the Peltola campaign, said the NYT reporting had supported findings by the state Division of Elections earlier this year.
paras.zh: 邓利维的声明没有透露佩尔托拉竞选活动的名称，称纽约时报的报道支持了州选举司今年早些时候的调查结果。

paras.en: "I am therefore directing the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether this scheme violated Alaska's laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted," he wrote. "The evidence will determine what happens next."
paras.zh: “因此，我指示公共安全部调查该计划是否违反了阿拉斯加州的法律，以及是否需要提起刑事指控或民事诉讼，”他写道。“证据将决定接下来会发生什么。”

paras.en: The NYT report alleged that people connected to Peltola's campaign, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), worked to try to recruit Sullivan the schoolteacher to stand in the Senate race.
paras.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，与佩尔托拉竞选活动有关的人，以及民主党参议院竞选委员会（ DSCC ）的高级助手，努力招募学校教师沙利文参加参议院竞选。

paras.en: This was part of a broader effort to encourage other would-be "spoiler" candidates to enter the race and dilute the support of the sitting Republican senator, the newspaper reported.
paras.zh: 据该报报道，这是鼓励其他潜在“破坏者”候选人参加竞选并淡化现任共和党参议员支持的更广泛努力的一部分。

paras.en: The paper said it had seen text messages and interviewed 12 people who participated in or were told of the plan, or were would-be candidates who the team tried to recruit. The BBC has not independently verified the NYT's reporting.
paras.zh: 该报称，它已经看到了短信，并采访了12名参与或被告知该计划的人，或者是该团队试图招募的潜在候选人。英国广播公司尚未独立核实纽约时报的报道。

paras.en: The DSCC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Dunleavy's investigation.
paras.zh: DSCC没有立即回复对Dunleavy的调查发表评论的请求。

paras.en: The ballot paper is set to list the two men as Dan S Sullivan, who will be described as the incumbent Republican senator, and Daniel J Sullivan Jr.
paras.zh: 选票上将列出两名男子，分别是丹·沙利文（ Dan S Sullivan ） ，他将被描述为现任共和党参议员，以及小丹尼尔· J ·沙利文（ Daniel J Sullivan Jr. ）。

paras.en: Senator Dan Sullivan told Fox News on Wednesday night that Peltola should "come clean" and described it as a scandal of the highest order.
paras.zh: 参议员丹·沙利文（ Dan Sullivan ）周三晚上告诉福克斯新闻，佩尔托拉应该“坦白” ，并将其描述为最高级别的丑闻。

paras.en: His fellow Republican senator in Alaska, Lisa Murkowksi, accused the Democratic campaign of engaging in a "pattern of lies". President Donald Trump has called for Peltola to be barred.
paras.zh: 他在阿拉斯加的共和党参议员丽莎·穆尔科克西（ Lisa Murkowksi ）指责民主党竞选活动存在“谎言模式”。唐纳德特朗普总统呼吁禁止佩尔托拉。

paras.en: Previous efforts by the Republicans to remove the non-incumbent Sullivan from the ballot have already been rejected by the Alaska Supreme Court which found no state laws had been broken by him running in the race.
paras.zh: 共和党人此前试图将非现任沙利文从选票中删除的努力已经被阿拉斯加最高法院驳回，该法院发现他在竞选中没有违反任何州法律。

paras.en: Though officials at the state and federal level have called for investigations in the wake of the New York Times reporting, election law experts said it was unlikely to dislodge the second Dan Sullivan from the ballot and it was unclear at this point if any state laws had been violated.
paras.zh: 尽管州和联邦一级的官员在《纽约时报》报道后呼吁进行调查，但选举法专家表示，不太可能将第二任丹·沙利文从选票中移除，目前尚不清楚是否有任何州法律被违反。

paras.en: "It turns out that convincing somebody to run for office is not a crime, even if their name happens to be the same as an incumbent," said Justin Levitt, an election law expert at Loyola Law School and a former justice department official.
paras.zh: “事实证明，说服某人竞选公职并不是犯罪，即使他们的名字恰好与现任者相同，”洛约拉法学院选举法专家、前司法部官员贾斯汀·莱维特（ Justin Levitt ）说。

paras.en: The non-incumbent Sullivan had a constitutional right to run and have his name on the ballot, added Ruth Greenwood, an election expert at Harvard Law School.
paras.zh: 哈佛法学院选举专家露丝·格林伍德（ Ruth Greenwood ）补充说，非现任沙利文（ Sullivan ）拥有参选并在选票上署名的宪法权利。

paras.en: The Trump administration filed a federal lawsuit last week aimed at preventing the certification of the result if the Trump-backed Sullivan loses, arguing that the presence of both of them on the ballot could confuse voters.
paras.zh: 特朗普政府上周提起了联邦诉讼，旨在阻止在特朗普支持的沙利文失败的情况下对结果进行认证，理由是他们在选票上的存在可能会让选民感到困惑。

paras.en: Some legal experts expressed scepticism of the merits of the lawsuit, and their chances of success given Alaska's courts had already allowed the second Sullivan to remain on the ballot.
paras.zh: 一些法律专家对诉讼的实质表示怀疑，鉴于阿拉斯加的法院已经允许第二位沙利文留在选票上，他们成功的机会。

paras.en: The actual legal arguments the justice department made were a "frivolous theory," Rick Pildes, an election law expert at New York University, told the BBC.
paras.zh: 纽约大学选举法专家里克·皮尔德斯（ Rick Pildes ）告诉英国广播公司，司法部提出的实际法律论点是一个“轻浮的理论”。

paras.en: He noted the lawsuit did not cite a specific provision that the government wanted to enforce, merely a general preamble taken from a sweeping US voting law.
paras.zh: 他指出，该诉讼没有引用政府想要执行的具体规定，只是摘自美国全面投票法的一般性序言。

paras.en: Alaska election officials asked a federal court to dismiss the lawsuit "because the complaint has no legal basis".
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加选举官员要求联邦法院驳回诉讼， “因为投诉没有法律依据”。

paras.en: The justice department has pledged continued action in the wake of the New York Times' reporting.
paras.zh: 在《纽约时报》报道之后，司法部已承诺继续采取行动。

paras.en: "They are cheating, let's call it what it is," Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Fox News on Wednesday.
paras.zh: “他们在作弊，让我们称之为它是什么，”司法部长托德布兰奇周三在福克斯新闻上说。

paras.en: In a series of Truth Social posts, Trump too pointed to the report and made a variety of allegations against Peltola, who he argued should be removed from the ballot. He repeated his endorsement for Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator, writing: "Dan is a GREAT man, has ALWAYS delivered for Alaska."
paras.zh: 在一系列真相社交帖子中，特朗普也指出了这份报告，并对佩尔托拉提出了各种指控，他认为佩尔托拉应该从选票中删除。他重申了他对现任共和党参议员Dan S Sullivan的支持，写道： “Dan是一个伟大的人，一直为阿拉斯加做出贡献。”

paras.en: Alaska's ranked-choice voting system means that voters could select both Sullivans if they are unsure at the ballot box.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加的排名投票系统意味着，如果选民在投票箱中不确定，他们可以选择两个沙利文。

paras.en: The battle threatens to delay the full picture of nationwide results following the midterm elections. The ultimate question of which party controls Congress will have a significant bearing on the remaining two years of Trump's presidency.
paras.zh: 这场战斗有可能推迟中期选举后的全国性结果的全貌。哪个政党控制国会的最终问题将对特朗普总统任期的剩余两年产生重大影响。

paras.en: A statement from an Alaskans for Mary spokesperson, written prior to Dunleavy's call for an investigation, said: "Mary got in this race because Alaskans deserve a champion who is fighting to lower their costs and put Alaska first, and no tweet or threat from any DC politician will keep her away from that fight.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加人为玛丽的发言人在邓利维呼吁进行调查之前发表的一份声明说： “玛丽参加了这场比赛，因为阿拉斯加人应该得到一个正在努力降低成本并把阿拉斯加放在第一位的冠军，任何华盛顿政治家的推文或威胁都不会让她远离这场斗争。

paras.en: "The Alaskans for Mary campaign has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign."
paras.zh: “阿拉斯加人为玛丽运动没有参与任何沙利文运动。”

paras.en: In a statement given to US media, the DSCC likewise denied that it had been involved in any such scheme.
paras.zh: 在向美国媒体发表的一份声明中， DSCC同样否认参与了任何此类计划。

paras.en: Peltola earlier this week paused campaigning activities in order to recover after she and her family sustained "minor injuries" in a car crash.
paras.zh: Peltola本周早些时候暂停了竞选活动，以便在她和她的家人在车祸中遭受“轻伤”后恢复过来。

articles.title: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit

paras.en: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has laid out her vision for what an "associate membership" status for Canada to the EU would look like as officials gather in Montreal to discuss closer ties.
paras.zh: 欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩（ Ursula von der Leyen ）提出了她的愿景，即随着官员们聚集在蒙特利尔讨论更紧密的联系，加拿大在欧盟的“准会员”地位会是什么样子。

paras.en: It is "a partnership that comes close to membership than anything we have done before," she said on Thursday's remarks at the two-day Canada-EU summit.
paras.zh: 她在周四为期两天的加拿大-欧盟峰会上发表讲话时表示，这是“一种比我们以前做过的任何事情都更接近成员国的伙伴关系”。

paras.en: She added it is a type of relationship that would be open "only to our closest partners outside of Europe who are ready to open a new frontier together."
paras.zh: 她补充说，这是一种关系， “只对准备共同开辟新领域的欧洲以外最亲密的合作伙伴开放”。

paras.en: It includes close alignment on governance and policies, and partnering in research and innovation.
paras.zh: 这包括在治理和政策方面的紧密结合，以及在研究和创新方面的合作。

paras.en: For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this year's meeting in the Canadian city.
paras.zh: 几十年来，加拿大-欧盟峰会没有大张旗鼓地举行-但今年在加拿大城市举行的会议并非如此。

paras.en: Thursday and Friday's summit is being closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.
paras.zh: 周四和周五的峰会正在密切关注有关加拿大和欧洲集团如何加深关系的细节。

paras.en: Von der Leyen first proposed "opening the door" to Canada last month for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.
paras.zh: 冯德莱恩上个月首次提出向加拿大“敞开大门” ，她称之为“准会员” -目前尚不存在这种身份。

paras.en: The overture came after Prime Minister Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, telling EU lawmakers that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".
paras.zh: 卡尼总理在斯特拉斯堡向欧洲议会发表讲话后表示，加拿大和欧洲在“地缘政治破裂”面前“更加强大”。

paras.en: Carney and many EU member states welcome closer ties, but not all are on board with what to call this new relationship.
paras.zh: 卡尼和许多欧盟成员国欢迎建立更紧密的联系，但并非所有国家都同意这种新关系的称呼。

paras.en: Some, like Germany, are questioning the "associate member" term, fearing that Canada is getting preferential treatment ahead of other nations who also want in.
paras.zh: 德国等一些国家正在质疑“准成员”一词，担心加拿大比其他也希望加入的国家获得优惠待遇。

paras.en: According to reports by multiple news outlets, Germany and other nations successfully lobbied to remove mention of the title in a draft statement ahead of the summit, opting instead for softer language that references an "ever closer association".
paras.zh: 根据多家新闻媒体的报道，德国和其他国家在峰会前成功游说删除了一份声明草案中对该标题的提及，而是选择了更温和的措辞，提及“更紧密的联系”。

paras.en: Germany's ambassador to Canada, Matthias LÃ¼ttenberg, told CTV News on Tuesday that some member states were "a little surprised" by von der Leyen's announcement last month.
paras.zh: 德国驻加拿大大使Matthias Lüttenberg周二告诉CTV新闻，一些成员国对冯德莱恩上个月的声明感到“有点惊讶”。

paras.en: While there is broad support for closer ties, the concept of "associate membership" is something that is not clearly understood as it pertains to Canada, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，虽然人们普遍支持建立更密切的联系，但“准会员”的概念并没有得到明确的理解，因为它与加拿大有关。

paras.en: "Germany has been using the term of associate membership for something completely different, which is the relationship of the EU to Ukraine and potentially Moldova", he said, both of which have been trying to join the bloc for many years.
paras.zh: 他说： “德国一直在使用准成员资格的术语，这是完全不同的，这是欧盟与乌克兰的关系，也可能与摩尔多瓦的关系。”这两个国家多年来一直试图加入欧盟。

paras.en: Despite some opposition, von der Leyen has continued to use the term has not addressed the disagreement over the term.
paras.zh: 尽管存在一些反对意见，但von der Leyen继续使用该术语并未解决该术语的分歧。

paras.en: Later on Thursday, Carney and von der Leyen and business leaders from both Europe and Canada will gather for a business forum.
paras.zh: 周四晚些时候，卡尼和冯德莱恩以及来自欧洲和加拿大的商界领袖将齐聚一堂，参加商业论坛。

paras.en: Canadian officials said they also expect agreements to be hammered out on defence, critical minerals, research and trade over the two days.
paras.zh: 加拿大官员表示，他们还预计将在两天内就国防、关键矿产、研究和贸易达成协议。

paras.en: Speaking to reporters earlier this week, European officials downplayed the possibility of a major announcement on Canada's new relationship with EU, saying much will be sorted in the coming months.
paras.zh: 本周早些时候，欧洲官员在接受记者采访时淡化了加拿大就与欧盟的新关系发表重大声明的可能性，称未来几个月将有很多问题得到解决。

paras.en: But both Canadian and EU officials have provided some clues on what the relationship could look like, including closer business ties and allowing more students to study on either side of the Atlantic.
paras.zh: 但加拿大和欧盟官员都提供了一些关于这种关系可能是什么样子的线索，包括更紧密的商业联系，并允许更多的学生在大西洋两岸学习。

paras.en: Canada also does not plan on paying a membership fee similar to other EU nations, Canadian officials have said. Instead, it is looking at participating in different EU programmes that would benefit both Canada and member states.
paras.zh: 加拿大官员表示，加拿大也不打算支付与其他欧盟国家类似的会员费。相反，它正在考虑加入不同的欧盟计划，这将使加拿大和成员国受益。

paras.en: And despite some disagreement about the wording, both have signalled they are fully on board with deepening ties.
paras.zh: 尽管对措辞存在一些分歧，但两人都表示他们完全支持加深联系。

paras.en: "The wording is emblematic of the ambition," said one senior Canadian official who was granted anonymity to speak to reporters at a briefing ahead of the summit.
paras.zh: 一位不愿透露姓名的加拿大高级官员在峰会前的简报会上对记者说： “措辞是这一雄心壮志的象征。”

paras.en: Polls show the majority of Canadians support forging closer ties to Europe, external, though the Conservative opposition in Canada has criticised the effort as a distraction from other issues, like the high cost of living.
paras.zh: 民意调查显示，大多数加拿大人支持与欧洲建立更紧密的外部关系，尽管加拿大的保守党反对派批评这项努力分散了对生活成本高等其他问题的注意力。

paras.en: "No one's mortgage or grocery bill will come down," said Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre in a statement, adding that Canada already has a free trade pact with the EU.
paras.zh: “没有人的抵押贷款或杂货账单会下降，”保守党领袖Pierre Poilievre在一份声明中表示，并补充说加拿大已经与欧盟签署了自由贸易协定。

paras.en: Since taking office last year, Prime Minister Carney has pushed Canada closer to Europe as his country continues to deal with an ongoing trade war with the US, its neighbour and largest trading customer.
paras.zh: 自去年上任以来，卡尼总理一直在推动加拿大更接近欧洲，因为他的国家继续应对与美国这个邻国和最大贸易客户的持续贸易战。

paras.en: US President Donald Trump has called the idea of Canada becoming an associate member of the EU "laughable", and has threatened "very serious tariffs" on Europe if he considered it a "hostile act".
paras.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（ Donald Trump ）称加拿大成为欧盟准成员的想法“可笑” ，并威胁称，如果他认为这是“敌对行为” ，将对欧洲征收“非常严重的关税”。

paras.en: Canadian officials stressed on Wednesday that their pivot to Europe is not meant to offend anybody, but rather to build on work that was already underway.
paras.zh: 加拿大官员周三强调，他们转向欧洲的目的不是要冒犯任何人，而是要在已经开展的工作的基础上再接再厉。

paras.en: Canada recently signed an agreement that gives its defence companies procurement access to the EU's Security and Defence Partnership programme.
paras.zh: 加拿大最近签署了一项协议，允许其国防公司采购欧盟的安全和防务伙伴关系计划。

paras.en: It also signed a landmark energy deal with Germany in May that would see the first-ever long-term shipments of liquified natural gas from Canada to Europe in the coming years.
paras.zh: 它还在5月与德国签署了一项具有里程碑意义的能源协议，该协议将在未来几年首次将液化天然气从加拿大长期运往欧洲。

paras.en: On Thursday, Canada released its new National Security Strategy, the first in two decades, which underlines supporting security and stability in Europe as a priority.
paras.zh: 周四，加拿大发布了新的国家安全战略，这是二十年来的首次，该战略强调将支持欧洲的安全与稳定作为优先事项。

paras.en: As for what this new relationship status will be called, Carney has said the "nomenclature" does not matter.
paras.zh: 至于这种新的关系状态将被称为什么，卡尼表示“命名法”并不重要。

paras.en: "What matters is the difference it will make to the lives of Canadians," he said.
paras.zh: “重要的是它将对加拿大人的生活产生影响，”他说。

articles.title: Visit Carlisle Brake & Friction at CONEXPO

paras.en: Visit Carlisle Brake & Friction at CONEXPO

Carlisle CBF will join our CentroMotion family at CONEXPO 2026 in booth #S82219 on the second level of the South Hall, where we will highlight our latest advancements in precision engineered braking systems.

Visitors will learn about our integrated combo park and service brake designed to deliver secure, high‑performance stopping capability; our new CBA50 Series service brake engineered for improved durability, efficiency, and serviceability in modern construction‑equipment platforms; our latest 1100 Series power valve with an electrohydraulic module and pedal that enhances control responsiveness; and our full lineup of EPD and N680, advanced friction‑material technologies tailored for a wide range of construction applications.

For Carlisle Brake & Friction, a CentroMotion brand, the week was an incredible opportunity to showcase innovation, strengthen partnerships and gain valuable insights into the future of the construction, mining and aggregate industries. Throughout the busy week, attendees had the chance to speak with our experts and watch live demonstrations of our brake systems, along with our advanced brake and transmission friction solutions for the construction industry.

articles.title: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

paras.en: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

Carlisle Brake & Friction has broken ground to expand its Chennai, India manufacturing operations in one of the world’s fastest-growing industrial regions. Having produced mechatronic products in the region for more than 15 years, Carlisle CBF will relocate to add production at a larger site for off-highway paper wet friction discs and steel separator plates. The new facility is scheduled to open in 2027.

The move to expanded space is designed to accommodate manufacturing capabilities needed to serve the growing demand across the agriculture, construction and especially mining industries in India and Southeast Asia. Local production will improve supply chain responsiveness while supporting original equipment and aftermarket requirements in cost-sensitive markets.

Carlisle Brake & Friction is establishing a state-of-the-art wet friction manufacturing facility on par with proven global manufacturing processes in the new Chennai plant, to build a more resilient regional platform. This expansion strengthens our ability to deliver durable wet friction products that help keep critical off-highway equipment productive.
